composition_notes: Keeps the workplace conservation setting and five-person evidence structure, includes six named evidence streams and distractor details, and avoids role-based, name-based, genre-based, or first-paragraph shortcuts. The target framing asks only for checksum selection and adds no external title or qualification.
intended_answer: Locally, “certified restoration lead” means the one participant whose relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol evidence statuses produce the incident’s accepted iterated modular checksum under the workshop’s rules. The premise deliberately does not identify that participant.
premise: At the Alder Street Conservation Workshop, a damaged lacquered astrolabe is being traced from the intake room through the imaging bay, solvent room, joinery room, records office, and quarantine vault. Five participants—Mara Venn, Ivo Sato, Nella Ortiz, Bram Keene, and Osei Ward—left overlapping annotations, tool checkouts, transit cards, timestamped messages, condition reports, and protocol acknowledgments during the examination. Several ordinary workshop details are irrelevant: supply deliveries, a broken lift, duplicate photographs, a visiting curator’s questions, a lunch-room key, and a mislabeled solvent crate. The workshop’s provenance ledger separates the useful observations into six evidence streams: relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol. For each participant, the local rules convert those six statuses into an ordered six-step iterated modular checksum; the accepted checksum is the one recorded for the incident after all ledger checks and room-to-room constraints are applied.
setting_summary: A conservation workshop traces a damaged artifact through several rooms while comparing participant records and provenance evidence.
target_question: Which participant is selected by the workshop’s accepted six-stream iterated modular checksum?
